description: Fig. 6 is a single-panel DSC (differential scanning calorimetry) line plot of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe alloys, x = 0/0.5/1.0/1.5 wt% Be, recorded on heating after homogenisation. The abscissa is "Temperature (°C)" running 1050 to 1350 with major ticks every 50 °C; the ordinate is "DSC (mW/mg)" with no printed numeric tick labels, so heat-flow magnitudes cannot be read. An arrow above the curves, labelled "Heating", marks the heating direction. Four curves are stacked with vertical offsets, so peak heights and areas are not directly comparable: magenta 1.5Be, blue 1.0Be, green 0.5Be and orange 0Be (legend, top right, lists exactly these four entries in that order). Each curve carries a printed peak annotation: 1.5Be = 1154.8 °C, 1.0Be = 1163.3 °C, 0.5Be = 1165.9 °C, and 0Be = 1320 °C, the last being a broad peak rising from roughly 1270 °C. The figure therefore shows that beryllium addition shifts the transformation peak of this alloy from a high-temperature event near 1320 °C to a cluster of closely spaced peaks between ~1155 and ~1166 °C. Note the citing text quotes 1278.8 °C for the Be-free steel, which the printed 1320 °C label does not match.

observations.observation: The figure is a single DSC panel with four vertically offset heating curves; the x-axis is labelled 'Temperature (°C)' and spans 1050 to 1350 with major ticks every 50 °C.
The y-axis is labelled 'DSC (mW/mg)' but carries no printed numeric tick values, so absolute heat-flow values cannot be read from the plot.
An arrow labelled 'Heating' above the curves indicates the heating direction (increasing temperature to the right).
The legend box in the top right lists four entries in this order: 1.5Be (magenta), 1.0Be (blue), 0.5Be (green), 0Be (orange).
Printed peak temperatures are 1154.8 °C for 1.5Be, 1163.3 °C for 1.0Be, 1165.9 °C for 0.5Be and 1320 °C for 0Be.
The three Be-containing peaks are clustered within 11.1 °C of one another (1154.8, 1163.3 and 1165.9 °C), whereas the Be-free peak lies far to the right at 1320 °C.
Peak temperature decreases monotonically with increasing Be content: 1165.9 °C (0.5Be) > 1163.3 °C (1.0Be) > 1154.8 °C (1.5Be).
The 0Be (orange) curve shows a broad endothermic-style peak whose rise begins at roughly 1270 °C and whose annotated apex is at 1320 °C, after which the signal falls steeply towards 1350 °C.
Because the four curves are offset vertically for display, their peak heights and peak areas cannot be compared quantitatively.
The caption states these are DSC heating curves of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe alloy after homogenisation.

The citing text states the phase transformation temperature of the steel without beryllium is 1278.8 °C, which disagrees with the 1320 °C peak label printed in the figure; both readings are reported here.
The citing text states that after adding Be the phase transformation point of the alloy steel decreased by approximately 120 °C.
The citing text states that at 1.0 wt% Be the transformation temperature decreased by approximately 1 °C relative to 0.5 wt% Be, and that at 1.5 wt% Be it decreased by 5 °C.
Both the figure and the citing text agree that beryllium addition strongly lowers the phase-transformation temperature of this Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C alloy.
